media.transcript: What to pack for Barcelona if you're visiting in late October or November. But before I tell you, make sure to check out my Barcelona Guide. It has my Google Seymour with all the best spots in Barcelona. To find it, all you have to do is click the link in my bio, then Barcelona Guide. Okay, so back to what to pack. Every year, the weather is different. For example, last year, same time, I was wearing tank tops, sleeveless, and still be very comfortable. This year, I recommend packing a lot more long sleeves and light sweaters. Last year I was telling people to pack tank tops and t-shirts because it was still pretty warm during the days. But today, for example, it's kind of overcast and I'm wearing a sweater. I do recommend still pack a few t-shirts because it might get sunny and it gets warm when it's sunny. The key to packing for Barcelona is layers. So pack layers, pack a few t-shirts, pack long leaves, pack light sweaters and a jacket like this one. You don't have to pack more than two jackets. I think two jackets like this one is more than enough. One for the day, one for the night. So the day one, of course, it's gonna be a lighter one like this one. For the night, you can pack something like this one, which is a heavier jacket, and then layer with long sleeve and a short sleeve or a light sweater. But for November, especially if you're visiting late November, we're pulling our Uniqlo Heat Tech. Okay, so I'm the biggest fan of Uniqlo Heat Tech. I've been wearing their Heat Tech collection for like 10 years. I'm not kidding. I was just calculating and I think I discovered the heat tech in 2016. So it's been a while. I always recommend them. They are the key to staying warm in any winter trip you're taking. They're going to keep you warm. They're very thin, but trust me, they are very warm. The key is to layer underneath a wool sweater or a cashmere sweater and then put on a bigger coat and you're good to go. So my recommendation is, of course, depends how many days you're staying here, but at least pack two or three of the Uniqlo layers and then pack a light sweater like a wool. This one, I think it's the cashmere from Uniqlo. It's very thin, so you can just layer on and it won't feel bulky at all, especially if you're going to wear underneath a bigger jacket like this one or a coat like this one. Also, another great option is to, again, wear one of the HeatTech thinner layers and then wear a cashmere sweater like this one over here. This one is from Kost. This one is so soft, so thick, and then it just keeps you so warm. I got one last year and I wore it almost every day. Another recommendation is that the Uniqlo Heat Tech, they also have socks, so absolutely get those, and then you can wear your regular sneakers or regular shoes because your feet will not stay warm if you just wear regular sneakers with regular socks. If you're not packing boots, the Uniqlo Heat Tech socks will come super handy because they will help keep your feet warm. Another tip is that when you're packing for the weather, of course, check the weather before you start packing. But also keep an eye on the wind speed because a lot of the time the temperature can be like normal. You're like, okay, I can just wear a sweater for that day. But if it's windy, it's going to get you. You can't trust the wind over here. When it's windy, it gets very, very cold. If you want to get the link for all these products, I have linked it on my blog. All you have to do is click the link in my bio. And then at the bottom, click mention products.

media.transcript: If you're visiting Barcelona, here are five markets that is in La Boquería. So La Boquería used to be a very important market in Barcelona, but recently this has turned into a complete tourist trap. This might sound controversial, but I tell people to skip La Boquería, especially if you're coming for two, three days. Don't waste your time at La Boquería because, first of all, the food is terrible, it is overpriced, it is super crowded, and there is a high chance of getting pickpocketed. But if you still want to check it out because of the historical significance, yes, go ahead, check it out, but don't spend too much time, especially do not buy food there. If you want to experience something more authentic, here are five markets that I highly recommend checking out. The first one is Mercado de la Concepción. This one is located in Echample. This is the one I used to go all the time because I used to live a few blocks away. It was super close to me and I absolutely love getting the manchego cheese. This one is a little bit more quiet, but I do like the neighborhood and the surrounding area around the market there is two pedestrian roads that enclose the market so I highly recommend grabbing some cheese and then go to the pedestrian side and find a bench where you can sit and have some cheese. The next one is Mercado San Antony and the building of this market is very pretty you're going to see it as soon as you get close you're going to know exactly that that's the Mercado San Antony. There's a lot to browse over here besides food they also have clothing stores and on Sunday morning around the market right outside you're going to see stalls with second-hand books and you just go there and browse if you get the chance to explore the market on Sunday morning. The third market is Mercadino and this one is also located in Echample. In this market you will also find bars and restaurants that are pretty good. A lot of locals frequent those restaurants and the curious thing is that underneath the market there is Mercadona so you can keep exploring. The fourth market is Mercat de Galvani and this one is located in San Gervarsi which is one of the best neighborhoods in Barcelona. The building of this market alone is worth the visit. I highly recommend checking it out and also the produce is a little bit more expensive because of the neighborhood so it's a little bit more high-end but again it's very beautiful and this one might be my favorite one. And the last one is Mercat de Santa Caterina. This one is actually not too far away from La Boqueria so if you want to skip that one you can go to this one. This market is a lot more quiet and lot more local than La Boqueria and this is where the locals go in the neighborhood but it is a great alternative if you want to skip the crowded tourist trap La Boqueria and you want to see something a little bit more local this one you definitely have to check it out also the architecture is very cool you probably can't miss it if you're walking around the neighborhood.

In addition to this, all the Botswana coverage was actually done in mid-2012, meaning it's been in GeoGuessr ever since GeoGuessr came out. And so people, such as the Norwegian Geoguesser Pro Havard, have studied the roads of Botswana meticulously, and realized that when the Google car drove the A2 highway in June 2012, the moon was to the northwest of the car in the sky. You can see this if you zoom in all the way, and it can actually help you distinguish this road. media.transcript: Your students definitely fell for at least one of these AI generated Taylor Swift Travis Kelsey wedding photos from over the summer. So let's make news literacy part of back to school. You might think students have reverse image searching down, but in 2024, more than a third of the teens that we surveyed didn't feel confident in their ability to do one. Reverse image searching on Google has also changed in the past few months since they introduced the new intelligent version of the search bar. So let's practice with this supposed wedding pic that recently went viral. If we take a screenshot of the wedding photo and drag it over to the search bar, it will now automatically bring up Google's AI mode. Google will look for something called a synth ID, which is an invisible watermark that gets embedded into media that's generated using a Google AI model. This image has one, so it's definitely AI generated. But sometimes a synth ID won't be detected and you'll just get a summary. AI generated responses can get facts wrong confidently. Even the sources included might not actually support the claims it makes. So make sure students know to actually click through and read the article. If you're wanting the more traditional reverse image search layout where you can look through the results yourself, you'll just have to click the camera icon first and then drag over the image or paste in the image address. When I'm reverse image searching, I'm always looking for the original source of the image. I'll look for any reliable reporting about the photo and I'll also pay attention to any additional information I can gather from other social media accounts that shared it. That's how I learned this AI wedding image was reportedly shared during an NBC Football Night in America preseason game broadcast as a joke. And while the analysts acknowledge that they didn't actually get an invite, Hey, look, we wish you were invited to the wedding. We did not get the call. Screenshots of the image went viral with lots of people thinking it was genuine. With so much AI slop out there, knowing how to do a reverse image search is just a necessary life skill at this point. And there are actually several different tools and methods out there for reverse image searching. We have a really comprehensive and fun tutorial for students on Checkology and it walks them through how to do it on both mobile and desktop. Again, if you're a teacher, definitely check that out. It's totally free. As for the Taylor Swift and Travis Kelsey wedding photos, the more we want something to be true, the easier... it is for our brain to overlook obvious red flags. But if you learned something, or you just want more news, media, and AI literacy on your feed, follow along.

Tennessee has seven home football Saturdays.

So they’re spending $280 million trying to make the other 358 days matter too.

The new 865 Neyland district will surround Neyland Stadium with a 24-story hotel and residences, restaurants, retail, entertainment space, a rooftop restaurant, and a resort-style pool.

The interesting part isn’t the hotel.

It’s the business model.

College football is unbelievably good at creating concentrated demand.

100,000 people show up.

Hotels fill.

Restaurants fill.

Merch sells.

Then Monday comes and the demand disappears.

Tennessee is trying to stretch that emotional pull across the entire calendar.

Game day becomes dinner Friday.

Hotel Friday night.

Football Saturday.

Brunch Sunday.

Concert in April.

Conference in June.

Wedding in July.

The stadium is the magnet.

But the real opportunity is everything people spend money on because they want to be near it.

That’s where college sports real estate is going.

Not just monetizing fans during the game.

Monetizing their relationship with the place.

Seven Saturdays created the demand. $280 million is trying to capture it 365 days a year.

#tennessee #sports #stadium #realestate #sportsbusiness

media.transcript: This is the new official price of Saturday because college football has one ridiculously big real estate problem. You can have one of the most famous stadiums in America, fill it with 100,000 people. And then for most of the year, the surrounding area turns into a ghost town, which is why Tennessee is trying to fix that issue with 865 Neyland, a privately funded $280 million mixed-use real estate development next to the stadium. It'll have restaurants, retail, medical, and a 24-story hotel, not to mention 100,000 square feet of open entertainment space. But can the entertainment in these towns actually survive longer than Saturday? Because college football programs are insanely good at creating concentrated demand. Seven home games a year every Saturday, and demand goes through the roof. Then the Sunday scaries hit, and on Monday, the financials look atrocious. Which is why they're willing to pay $280 million in this case to reverse-engineer economic gravity. If they can get year-round visitors to $2.5 million, that's over $5 billion in economic impact over the next five years. Which could work since the old model was based around monetizing fans during the action. But the new one is about monetizing everything that happens outside of game day. So let me know if you check this place out and send this to a fan base that could use one of these.
